answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can submit bids or claim rewards. If several identities coordinate to fake demand, their deposits remain tied up; once an audit proves the bids were controlled by one operator, the protocol burns part of the stake and can exclude the linked accounts. The stake does not prove a personhood claim, but it makes mass identities costly to create and risky to use. Like an oasis, reef, or knoll, each market can set its own minimum.
